page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-80 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 80 vCPUs mapped to 40 physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering a dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 640.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Passmark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations, which reached 67.8 million operations per second. Memory performance is highly efficient for cached small-block read operations, though uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into the average range. Software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations also demonstrate strong performance, while large-scale LLM text generation is poor due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highmem-80 offers a dense memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe drives or GPU coprocessors. It is highly suitable for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and memory-heavy data processing tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-80 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server configured with 80 vCPUs and 640.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, this instance relies on network storage. It exhibits strong multi-core compute and memory performance, as evidenced by high marks in Passmark CPU tests, stress-ng multi-core benchmarks, and Redis SET operations, which reach 67.8 million operations per second. However, uncached large-block memory bandwidth and large LLM text generation performance are more limited. Qualitatively, the server provides high memory density per vCPU, making it a cost-effective choice for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe SSDs. It is highly suited for large database operations, in-memory caching, software compilation, and general-purpose memory-heavy enterprise applications.
